title: Return the trusts
hookLine: return trusts to their owners and judge with justice (4:58)

cards: Mecca, the day the Muslims entered the city after years of exile. The Prophet ﷺ goes to the Ka'bah, and the key to its door is brought to him from Uthman ibn Talhah, whose family kept it.

Now the key is in the hand of the man who controls the city. Someone from his own family, his uncle al-Abbas in some reports, asks for the honor of holding it. Everyone is watching to see who gets the key.

teach.b: Commentators report that he came out of the Ka'bah reciting 4:58. In Pickthall's words: "Lo! Allah commandeth you that ye restore deposits to their owners, and, if ye judge between mankind, that ye judge justly."
And he gave the key back to Uthman ibn Talhah, saying it would stay with his family. Tradition says it has stayed with that family, the Banu Shaybah, ever since.
The Arabic for deposits is amanat, trusts: anything placed in your care. The root is the same as iman, faith, and amn, safety.
A trust is a small piece of safety someone hands you. This wasn't new for the Prophet.
The sira says that before his prophethood, Meccans called him al-Amin, the trustworthy, and left their valuables with him, and kept doing it even when they turned against him.
On the night he left Mecca for Medina, with enemies at his door, the sira reports he left Ali behind to return every deposit to its owner.
Scholars read the verse widely: a loan, a secret, a borrowed book, a job you were hired to do, a public office.
The second half, judge justly, they read as a trust too: power over others is placed in your hands for a while, and owed back.
A hadith in Bukhari lists among the signs of a hypocrite: when trusted, he betrays. A key, a lent jacket, a secret, a job. Whatever was put in your hands for a while, give it back whole.

how: Muslims treat amanah, trustworthiness, as a core trait of faith, covering loans, deposits, secrets, work and public office; the key of the Ka'bah is traditionally held by the Banu Shaybah, the family of Uthman ibn Talhah.

games.q: you've just taken the city. the key to its holiest door is in your hand, and someone from your own family asks for it. what does the Prophet do?

return it to Uthman ibn Talhah's family.
games.why: he gave it back to Uthman ibn Talhah, saying it would stay with his family. tradition says it has stayed there.

practice: Take a slow inventory of what you're holding that isn't yours: a book, a dish from a neighbor, a charger, money someone lent you, a secret someone told you, a job you said you'd finish.
Let each come to mind without guilt, then picture handing one back, whole, with a thank-you.

wordCard.voice: Amanah, a trust, anything placed in your care. Restore the amanat to their owners, and judge justly, from 4:58: the verse recited with the key to the Ka'bah. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the trusts, deposits (4:58); singular amanah, from the root of iman and amn, safety.
